title: Silent Terror
stack: Angular · Python / FastAPI · MySQL · Docker · SVM · Fuzzy Logic · Ollama
description:
An ongoing social-deduction game project exploring how intent classification, fuzzy reasoning, and language models can work together to generate contextual AI dialogue.

As team lead, full-stack developer, and AI researcher, I contribute to project coordination, application development, database and Docker setup, and AI experimentation.

The current repository documents room-based multiplayer, role actions, timed phases, voting, and win conditions. The game engine controls the rules, while the AI pipeline supports NOX conversation.
role: Team Lead · Full-stack Developer · AI Researcher

ai.approach: Classify chat intent with SVM, convert behavioral signals into fuzzy suspicion scores, then pass that context to an LLM for role-aware dialogue. Explore local CPU/GPU inference alongside an OpenAI API option.
ai.output: NOX bot dialogue informed by chat intent, suspicion scores, and game context.
ai.evaluation: Ongoing prototype: inspect each stage through pipeline traces. Bot actions and votes use rules; the LLM generates dialogue. The fuzzy silence input is currently fixed rather than measured.

title: Mushroom Vision
stack: React · Python / Flask · TensorFlow / Keras · OpenCV · scikit-learn
description:
A computer vision course project that classifies mushroom photos through an interactive React interface. Upload an image to receive a predicted class, confidence score, and descriptive information.

The Flask API extracts color, texture, shape, and keypoint features with OpenCV and scikit-image, scales them, and passes them to a trained TensorFlow/Keras CNN. The model works with extracted features rather than raw image pixels.

I built the frontend for this collaborative university project, connecting the image-upload and analysis experience to the prediction API.

ai.approach: Resize images to 128 x 128 and extract HSV color histograms, GLCM, Hu moments, HOG, LBP, and FAST statistics. Scale the resulting feature vector before CNN inference; the CNN receives features rather than raw pixels.
ai.output: Predicted mushroom class, per-image confidence score, and descriptive metadata.
ai.evaluation: The confidence score describes an individual prediction, not overall accuracy. The repository documents multiple experiment iterations but its README does not report a benchmark score.

title: Diebety AI Predict
description: An AI diabetes-risk predictor using logistic regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, preprocessing, SHAP feature selection, and Streamlit.

ai.approach: Explore tabular diabetes-risk classification with data preprocessing and multiple supervised learning models, using SHAP-based feature analysis to examine the contribution of input features.
ai.output: A Streamlit application that returns a diabetes-risk prediction from user inputs.
ai.evaluation: The project profile reports approximately 90% classification accuracy. The available summary does not identify the winning model, evaluation split, or per-model scores.

title: SkolioCheck
description: A CNN-based VGG16 deep-learning project for scoliosis detection using X-ray images.

ai.focus: Computer Vision · Deep Learning · Medical Imaging
ai.approach: Apply a VGG16-based CNN to X-ray classification. The Flask inference app converts uploads to RGB, resizes them to 224 x 224, normalizes pixels to 0-1, and applies a 0.6 threshold to the model output.
ai.output: An X-ray classification result: Normal Detected or Scoliosis Detected.
ai.evaluation: A research prototype. No verified accuracy, sensitivity, or specificity figures are included in the available project documentation.
